about: Levels and steps in teaching order, through the end of first grade. Each step lists the letters and letter groups (graphemes) it introduces, and a name for the parent screens. A word belongs to the first step by which all its letters have been introduced, unless it names a later step itself: blends, endings, and two-syllable words bring no new letters, so their words carry their step. a_e is the split vowel in make; endings (es, ing, ed) are taught as units.

levels.summary: Short a, then short i; consonants b, c, d, f, g, h, l, m, n, p, r, s, t
Short o, then u, then e; consonants j, k, v, w, x, y, z
Letter pairs: sh, ch, th, wh, ck, ff, ll, ss, zz, qu, ng, nk

steps.name: ck, ff, ll, ss, zz, and qu
blends with s and l (stop, clap)
blends at the end (best, hand, jump)

levels.summary: Silent e: make, bike, home, cute

steps.name: o and u with silent e (home, cute)

levels.summary: Vowel teams and vowels with r: ee, ea, ai, ay, oa, ow, ar, or, er, ir, ur

steps.name: er, ir, and ur (her, bird, fur)

levels.summary: Endings (dogs, wishes, jumping, jumped) and two-syllable words (sunset)
